stories.title: 📜 2 एज्रा (4 एज्रा) 1
summaryBullets: बंधुआई में सरायाह के पुत्र एज्रा के पास प्रभु का वचन आता है (1:1-3)।
परमेश्वर इस्राएल को अवज्ञा के लिए फटकार लगाता है, मिस्र से छुटकारे और सीनै की वाचा का स्मरण कराता है, फिर भी उनके निरंतर विद्रोह को बताता है (1:4-25)।
इस्राएल को कहा जाता है कि अविश्वासयोग्यता के कारण उन्हें अस्वीकार किया जाएगा, परंतु एक नया लोग उठेगा जो परमेश्वर का आदर करेगा (1:26-40)।
crossRefs: व्यवस्थाविवरण 32:15-20 — इस्राएल की अविश्वासयोग्यता।
होशे 1:9-10 — 'मेरी प्रजा नहीं' फिर भी पुनर्स्थापित।
प्रकाशितवाक्य 7:9-17 — श्वेत वस्त्र पहने भीड़।

translationNotes.note: न्याय और पुरस्कार के दर्शनों में धर्मियों को दिया जाने वाला सम्मान और प्रतिफल का प्रतीक।

stories.keyTakeaway: परमेश्वर इस्राएल की अवज्ञा की फटकार लगाता है, न्याय की प्रतिज्ञा करता है और एक विश्वासयोग्य शेषांश को न्याय की आशा से सांत्वना देता है।

stories.title: 📜 2 एज्रा (4 एज्रा) 2
summaryBullets: विश्वासयोग्य लोगों को प्रोत्साहन दिया जाता है: 'मेरे लोगों, मेरे वचन सुनो,' न्याय की प्रतिज्ञाओं के साथ (2:1-32)।
सिय्योन का एक दर्शन माता के रूप में अपनी संतानों को सांत्वना देता है; धर्मियों को आनंद, मुकुट और अनंत विश्राम की प्रतिज्ञा दी जाती है (2:33-48)।

stories.title: 🌿 2 एज्रा (4 एज्रा) 3
summaryBullets: एज्रा सिय्योन के विनाश पर विलाप करता है और प्रश्न करता है कि इस्राएल क्यों पीड़ित है जबकि बाबुल समृद्ध है (3:1-36)।
crossRefs: हबक्कूक 1:2-4 — दुष्ट क्यों समृद्ध होते हैं?
दानिय्येल 12:4 — ज्ञान अंत तक मुहरबंद।

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אוּרִיאֵל (ʾŪriʾēl, 'God is my light') — Greek: Οὐριὴλ (Ouriēl) — Aramaic: אוריאל (ʾŪriʾēl)
translationNotes.note: 2 एज्रा में दर्शनों के व्याख्याकार के रूप में भेजा गया प्रधान स्वर्गदूत, यहूदी रहस्यवादी परंपराओं में भी नामित।

stories.keyTakeaway: एज्रा इस्राएल की पीड़ा पर विलाप करता है; ऊरीएल प्रकट करता है कि परमेश्वर के छिपे उद्देश्य इतिहास को संचालित करते हैं और अंत चिह्नों के साथ आएगा।

stories.title: 🌿 2 एज्रा (4 एज्रा) 4
summaryBullets: स्वर्गदूत ऊरीएल उत्तर देने के लिए भेजा जाता है, सिखाता है कि मानवीय समझ परमेश्वर के सभी मार्गों को नहीं समझ सकती (4:1-21)।
दर्शन अंत का वर्णन करते हैं: अग्नि, अराजकता और प्रकृति में चिह्न; इस्राएल की कठिनाइयों को परमेश्वर की योजना में समझाया गया है (4:22-52)।

stories.title: 📜 2 एज्रा (4 एज्रा) 6
summaryBullets: एज्रा लिव्यातान और बहेमोत के दर्शन देखता है, अंत के लिए तैयार किए गए आदिम प्राणी (6:47-52)।

summaryBullets: वर्तमान युग के अंत और अगले युग के आरंभ का प्रकाशन, जब न्याय आएगा (7:26-44)।

stories.title: 📜 2 एज्रा (4 एज्रा) 8
summaryBullets: He answered me and said, “The Most High made this world for the sake of many but the world to come for the sake of only a few. (8:1).

But I tell you a parable, Ezra. Just as, when you ask the earth, it will tell you that it provides a large amount of clay from which earthenware is made but only a little dust from which gold comes, so is the course of the present world. (8:2).
Many have been created, but only a few shall be saved.” (8:3).
I answered and said, “Then drink your fill of understanding, O my soul, and drink wisdom, O my heart. (8:4).
For not of your own will did you come into the world, and against your will you depart, for you have been given only a short time to live. (8:5).

O Lord above us, grant to your servant that we may pray before you, and give us a seed for our heart and cultivation of our understanding so that fruit may be produced, by which every mortal who bears the likeness of a human may be able to live. (8:6).
For you alone exist, and we are a work of your hands, as you have declared. (8:7).

And because you give life to the body that is now fashioned in the womb and furnish it with members, what you have created is preserved amid fire and water, and for nine months the womb endures your creature that has been created in it. (8:8).
But that which keeps and that which is kept shall both be kept by your keeping. And when the womb gives up again what has been created in it, (8:9).
you have commanded that from the members themselves (that is, from the breasts) milk, the fruit of the breasts, should be supplied, (8:10).
so that what has been fashioned may be nourished for a time, and afterward you will still guide it in your mercy. (8:11).
You have nurtured it in your righteousness and instructed it in your law and reproved it in your wisdom. (8:12).
You put it to death as your creation and make it live as your work. (8:13).
If then you will suddenly and quickly destroy what with so great labor was fashioned by your command, to what purpose was it made? (8:14).
And now I will speak out: About all humankind you know best, but I will speak about your people, for whom I am grieved, (8:15).
and about your inheritance, for whom I lament, and about Israel, for whom I am sad, and about the seed of Jacob, for whom I am troubled. (8:16).
Therefore I will pray before you for myself and for them, for I see the failings of us who inhabit the earth, (8:17).
and now also I have heard of the swiftness of the judgment that is to come. (8:18).
Therefore hear my voice and understand my words, and I will speak before you.” The beginning of the words of Ezra’s prayer, before he was taken up. He said: (8:19).
“O Lord, you who inhabit eternity, whose eyes are exalted and whose upper chambers are in the air, (8:20).
whose throne is beyond measure and whose glory is beyond comprehension, before whom the hosts of angels stand trembling (8:21).
and at whose command they are changed to wind and fire, whose word is sure and whose utterances are certain, whose command is strong and whose ordinance is terrible, (8:22).
whose look dries up the depths and whose indignation makes the mountains melt away, and whose truth is established forever — (8:23).
hear, O Lord, the prayer of your servant, and give ear to the petition of your creature; attend to my words. (8:24).
For as long as I live I will speak, and as long as I have understanding I will answer. (8:25).
O do not look on the sins of your people but on those who serve you in truth. (8:26).
Do not take note of the endeavors of those who act wickedly but of the endeavors of those who have kept your covenants amid afflictions. (8:27).
Do not think of those who have lived wickedly in your sight, but remember those who have willingly acknowledged that you are to be feared. (8:28).
Do not will the destruction of those who have the ways of cattle, but regard those who have gloriously taught your law. (8:29).
Do not be angry with those who are deemed worse than wild animals, but love those who have always put their trust in your glory. (8:30).
For we and our ancestors have passed our lives in ways that bring death, but it is because of us sinners that you are called merciful. (8:31).
For if you have desired to have pity on us, who have no works of righteousness, then you will be called merciful. (8:32).
For the righteous, who have many works laid up with you, shall receive their reward in consequence of their own deeds. (8:33).
But what are mortals that you are angry with them, or what is a corruptible race that you are so bitter against it? (8:34).
For in truth there is no one among those who have been born who has not acted wickedly; among those who have existed there is no one who has not done wrong. (8:35).
For in this, O Lord, your righteousness and goodness will be declared: when you are merciful to those who have no store of good works.” (8:36).
He answered me and said, “Some things you have spoken rightly, and it will turn out according to your words. (8:37).
For indeed I will not concern myself about the fashioning of those who have sinned or about their death, their judgment, or their destruction, (8:38).
but I will rejoice over the creation of the righteous, over their pilgrimage also, and their salvation, and their receiving their reward. (8:39).
As I have spoken, therefore, so it shall be. (8:40).

“For just as the farmer sows many seeds in the ground and plants a multitude of seedlings and yet not all that have been sown will come up in due season and not all that were planted will take root, so also those who have been sown in the world will not all be saved.” (8:41).
I answered and said, “If I have found favor in your sight, let me speak. (8:42).
If the farmer’s seed does not come up because it has not received your rain in due season or if it has been ruined by too much rain, it perishes. (8:43).

But people, who have been formed by your hands and are called your own image because they are made like you and for whose sake you have formed all things, have you also made them like the farmer’s seed? (8:44).
Surely not, O Lord above! But spare your people and have mercy on your inheritance, for you have mercy on your own creation.” (8:45).
He answered me and said, “Things that are present are for those who live now, and things that are future are for those who will live hereafter. (8:46).
For you come far short of being able to love my creation more than I love it. But you have often compared yourself to the unrighteous. Never do so! (8:47).
But even in this respect you will be praiseworthy before the Most High, (8:48).
because you have humbled yourself, as is becoming for you, and have not considered yourself to be among the righteous. You will receive the greatest glory, (8:49).
for many miseries will affect those who inhabit the world in the last times because they have walked in great pride. (8:50).
But think of your own case, and inquire concerning the glory of those who are like yourself, (8:51).

because it is for you that paradise is opened, the tree of life is planted, the age to come is prepared, plenty is provided, a city is built, rest is appointed, goodness is established, and wisdom is perfected beforehand. (8:52).
The root of evil is sealed up from you, illness is banished from you, and death is hidden; Hades has fled, and corruption has been forgotten; (8:53).
sorrows have passed away, and in the end the treasure of immortality is made manifest. (8:54).
Therefore do not ask any more questions about the great number of those who perish. (8:55).
For when they had opportunity to choose, they despised the Most High and were contemptuous of his law and abandoned his ways. (8:56).
Moreover, they have even trampled on his righteous ones (8:57).
and said in their hearts that there is no God—though they knew well that they must die. (8:58).
For just as the things that I have predicted await you, so the thirst and torment that are prepared await them. For the Most High did not intend that anyone should be destroyed, (8:59).
but those who were created have themselves defiled the name of him who made them and have been ungrateful to him who prepared life for them now. (8:60).
Therefore my judgment is now drawing near; (8:61).
I have not shown this to all people but only to you and a few like you.” Then I answered and said, (8:62).
“O Lord, you have already shown me a great number of the signs that you will do in the last times, but you have not shown me when you will do them.” (8:63).

stories.title: 📜 2 एज्रा (4 एज्रा) 9
summaryBullets: अंत से पहले के चिह्नों में सृष्टि में उथल-पुथल, अकाल और राष्ट्रों में अशांति शामिल है (9:1-12)।
थोड़े से धर्मी लोगों की तुलना नाश होने वाले बहुतों से की जाती है; एज्रा इस्राएल के लिए शोक से जूझता है (9:13-25)।
एज्रा एक शोकाकुल स्त्री को देखता है जो अपने इकलौते पुत्र की मृत्यु पर विलाप कर रही है (9:26-44)।

stories.title: 📜 2 एज्रा (4 एज्रा) 13
summaryBullets: After seven days I dreamed a dream in the night. (13:1).
And behold, a wind arose from the sea and stirred up all its waves. (13:2).

As I kept looking the wind made something like the figure of a man come up out of the heart of the sea. And I saw that this man flew with the clouds of heaven, and wherever he turned his face to look, everything under his gaze trembled, (13:3).
and whenever his voice issued from his mouth, all who heard his voice melted as wax melts when it feels the fire. (13:4).
After this I looked and saw that an innumerable multitude of people were gathered together from the four winds of heaven to make war against the man who came up out of the sea. (13:5).
And I looked and saw that he carved out for himself a great mountain and flew up on to it. (13:6).
And I tried to see the region or place from which the mountain was carved, but I could not. (13:7).
After this I looked and saw that all who had gathered together against him to wage war with him were filled with fear, yet they dared to fight. (13:8).
When he saw the onrush of the approaching multitude, he neither lifted his hand nor held a spear or any weapon of war, (13:9).

but I saw only how he sent forth from his mouth something like a stream of fire and from his lips a flaming breath and from his tongue he shot forth a storm of sparks. All these were mingled together, the stream of fire and the flaming breath and the great storm, (13:10).

and fell on the onrushing multitude that was prepared to fight and burned up all of them, so that suddenly nothing was seen of the innumerable multitude but only the dust of ashes and the smell of smoke. When I saw it, I was amazed. (13:11).
After this I saw the same man come down from the mountain and call to himself another multitude that was peaceable. (13:12).

Then the forms of many people appeared to him, some of whom were joyful and some sorrowful; some of them were bound, and some were bringing others as offerings. Then I woke up in great terror and prayed to the Most High and said, (13:13).
“From the beginning you have shown your servant these wonders and have deemed me worthy to have my prayer heard by you; (13:14).
now show me the interpretation of this dream also. (13:15).
For as I consider it in my mind, alas for those who will be left in those days! And still more, alas for those who are not left! (13:16).
For those who are not left will be sad (13:17).
because they understand the things that are reserved for the last days but cannot attain them. (13:18).
But alas for those also who are left and for that very reason! For they shall see great dangers and much distress, as these dreams show. (13:19).
Yet it is better to come into these things, though incurring peril, than to pass from the world like a cloud and not to see what will happen in the last days.” He answered me and said, (13:20).
“I will tell you the interpretation of the vision, and I will also explain to you the things that you have mentioned. (13:21).
As for what you said about those who survive, and concerning those who do not survive, this is the interpretation: (13:22).
The one who brings the peril at that time will protect those who fall into peril, who have works and faith toward the Almighty. (13:23).
Understand, therefore, that those who are left are more blessed than those who have died. (13:24).
“This is the interpretation of the vision: As for your seeing a man come up from the heart of the sea, (13:25).
this is he whom the Most High has been keeping for many ages, who will himself deliver his creation, and he will direct those who are left. (13:26).
And as for your seeing wind and fire and a storm coming out of his mouth (13:27).
and as for his not holding a spear or weapon of war, yet destroying the onrushing multitude that came to conquer him, this is the interpretation: (13:28).
The days are coming when the Most High will deliver those who are on the earth. (13:29).
And bewilderment of mind shall come over those who inhabit the earth. (13:30).
They shall plan to make war against one another, city against city, place against place, people against people, and kingdom against kingdom. (13:31).
When these things take place and the signs occur that I showed you before, then my Son will be revealed, whom you saw as a man coming up from the sea. (13:32).
“Then, when all the nations hear his voice, all the nations shall leave their own lands and the warfare that they have against one another, (13:33).
and an innumerable multitude shall be gathered together, as you saw, wishing to come and conquer him. (13:34).
But he shall stand on the top of Mount Zion. (13:35).
And Zion shall come and be made manifest to all people, prepared and built, as you saw the mountain carved out without hands. (13:36).
Then he, my Son, will reprove the assembled nations for their ungodliness (this was symbolized by the storm) (13:37).

and will reproach them to their face with their evil thoughts and the torments with which they are to be tortured (which were symbolized by the flames) and will destroy them without effort by means of the law (which was symbolized by the fire). (13:38).
“And as for your seeing him gather to himself another multitude that was peaceable, (13:39).

these are the nine tribes that were taken away from their own land into exile in the days of King Hoshea, whom Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, made captives; he took them across the river, and they were taken into another land. (13:40).
But they formed this plan for themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the nations and go to a more distant region where no humans had ever lived, (13:41).
so that there at least they might keep their statutes that they had not kept in their own land. (13:42).
And they went in by the narrow passages of the River Euphrates. (13:43).
For at that time the Most High performed signs for them and stopped the channels of the river until they had crossed over. (13:44).
Through that region there was a long way to go, a journey of a year and a half, and that country is called Arzareth. (13:45).
“Then they lived there until the last times, and now, when they are about to come again, (13:46).
the Most High will stop the channels of the river again, so that they may be able to cross over. Therefore you saw the multitude gathered together in peace. (13:47).
But those who are left of your people, who are found within my holy borders, shall be saved. (13:48).
Therefore when he destroys the multitude of the nations that are gathered together, he will defend the people who remain. (13:49).
And then he will show them very many wonders.” (13:50).
I said, “O sovereign Lord, explain this to me: Why did I see the man coming up from the heart of the sea?” (13:51).
He said to me, “Just as no one can explore or know what is in the depths of the sea, so no one on earth can see my Son or those who are with him, except in the time of his day. (13:52).
This is the interpretation of the dream that you saw. And you alone have been enlightened about this, (13:53).
because you have forsaken your own ways and have applied yourself to mine and have searched out my law, (13:54).
for you have devoted your life to wisdom and called understanding your mother. (13:55).

Therefore I have shown you these things, for there is a reward laid up with the Most High. For it will be that after three more days I will tell you other things and explain weighty and wondrous matters to you.” (13:56).
Then I got up and walked in the field, giving great glory and praise to the Most High for the wonders that he did from time to time (13:57).
and because he governs the times and whatever things come to pass in their seasons. And I stayed there three days. (13:58).

summaryBullets: परमेश्वर एज्रा को आज्ञा देता है कि संसार पर आने वाली महामारियों, अकाल, तलवार और विनाश की घोषणा करे (15:1-27)।
मिस्र, सीरिया, बाबुल और एशिया को पाप और घमंड के कारण विपत्तियों के लिए चिह्नित किया गया है (15:28-46)।
पृथ्वी और उसके शासक परमेश्वर के न्याय पर काँपते हैं; युद्ध, अकाल और महामारी फैलती है (15:47-63)।

प्रकाशितवाक्य 16:1-21 — क्रोध के कटोरे उंडेले गए।

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מַכָּה (makkāh) — Greek: πληγαί (plēgaí) — Aramaic: מכתא (maktāʾ)
translationNotes.note: ईश्वरीय न्याय के प्रहार, जो राष्ट्रों पर अकाल, तलवार, अग्नि और महामारी के रूप में वर्णित हैं।

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צָרָה (ṣārāh) — Greek: θλῖψις (thlîpsis) — Aramaic: עקתא (ʿoqtāʾ)
translationNotes.note: गंभीर कष्ट या दबाव; यहाँ परीक्षा का समय जिसमें विश्वासयोग्य लोगों से दृढ़ बने रहने का आग्रह किया गया है।

stories.keyTakeaway: 2 एज्रा राष्ट्रों के विरुद्ध न्याय के सर्वनाश दर्शनों और विश्वासयोग्य लोगों के लिए परमेश्वर पर भरोसा रखते हुए क्लेश सहने के आह्वान के साथ समाप्त होता है।
